title: First full training pass produces a checkpoint that passes numerical retention

data.title: First full training pass produces a checkpoint that passes numerical retention
paragraphs: At update 294,740, the second of six fixed native comparisons is the first to pass every frozen numerical guard. Equal-weight nine-cohort development WER falls from the preserved initial model's 18.511% to 17.805%, an absolute reduction of 0.706 percentage points. Seven cohorts improve and two regress. The saved development summary provisionally lists step 294,740 as the best eligible checkpoint; selection remains unfinished until all six comparisons complete. The initial model remains default and no automatic promotion occurs.

One complete pass has visited all 2,052,751 qualified training microphone views, representing 220,174 distinct source utterances. Visits/distinct sources are Common Voice 91,123/91,123; AMI 682,812/76,795; CHiME-6 1,261,887/51,743; and VOiCES 16,929/513. Training starts from the pinned pretrained base and updates all 55,151,433 parameters. Original four-domain objective weights and source/quiet confidence rules remain unchanged; development and evaluation stay excluded.

WER and saved candidate-minus-initial uncertainty for the noisy and age cohorts: AMI 26.825% to 25.361% (-1.464 points; 95% interval [-4.430, +1.211]); CHiME-6 76.320% to 74.142% (-2.178 points; 95% interval [-8.029, +3.725]); Common Voice age 12.286% to 12.042% (-0.244 points; 95% interval [-1.794, +1.240]). AMI and CHiME-6 both improve in their aggregate point estimates, but their meeting/session intervals still include regression.

The earlier clean-speech guard failure is resolved at this checkpoint: CMU Arctic clean 8.541% to 8.185% (-0.356 points; 95% interval [-1.903, +1.094]). Also, HiFiTTS clean 7.485% to 6.713% (-0.772 points; 95% interval [-1.124, -0.525]); HiFiTTS native 6.464% to 5.627% (-0.837 points; 95% interval [-1.812, -0.131]). The HiFiTTS development intervals are fragile because clean has only two readers and native four.

The two WER regressions are LibriSpeech clean 5.894% to 5.975% (+0.081 points; 95% interval [-0.739, +0.948]); and LibriSpeech native 10.269% to 10.583% (+0.314 points; 95% interval [-0.872, +1.419]). Their increases remain within the frozen clean/native limits. VOiCES 12.511% to 11.613% (-0.898 points; 95% interval [-1.873, +0.180]); its evidence remains sparse at 26 source utterances, 78 views and 13 speakers. Equal aggregate VOiCES WER at steps 147,370 and 294,740 does not imply identical errors: the saved uncertainty interval differs and now includes no improvement.

The saved 10,000-draw paired cluster-bootstrap interval for the nine-cohort WER change is [-1.506, +0.075] percentage points. It includes zero, so passing the numerical selection gates does not establish a statistically clear overall gain. The bootstrap averages microphone views per source and resamples meetings, sessions or speakers. These exploratory development intervals are not adjusted for choosing among six checkpoints.

Microphone slices still expose a substantial regression hidden by aggregate CHiME-6 improvement: array WER changes from 79.212% to 76.970%, while worn-microphone WER rises from 41.606% to 54.745% on 27 clips, unchanged from the first checkpoint. AMI array WER improves from 31.859% to 30.966% and headset from 17.804% to 15.668%. These slices are descriptive, have no saved slice-specific intervals, and do not alter the frozen selection policy.

Quiet-speech WER rises from 31.823% to 32.395%, a 0.573-point regression on 160 views, 77 sources and 1,004 reference words. Its saved 95% change interval is [-3.121, +5.610] points. The point estimate remains within the 1.0-point guard, but quiet-speech improvement is not established. Both models still produce zero false positives and zero inserted words on the 20 silence/noise probes; these limited probes do not establish intelligibility or product-microphone performance.

The owned pipeline has resumed its second training pass toward update 442,110. Four fixed comparisons remain before a single development candidate can be frozen; confirmation will not choose a runner-up. Both evaluation panels reuse previously evaluated populations rather than providing fresh independent confirmation. HiFiTTS clean confirmation has only one reader, leaving its interval and the complete nine-cohort confirmation interval undefined. There is still no real product-microphone validation or independent final age test. Earlier model identities remain preserved; the new checkpoint remains experimental.
